chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for a man that the Jewish woman, the Christian woman, and the polytheist woman breastfeed him?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem,' and he said, 'Prevent them from drinking wine.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding by a Jewish or Christian woman establish mahram relations for a man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that breastfeeding by women of the People of the Book or polytheists is legally valid (*sahih*) for establishing *mahram* kinship, countering views that might restrict it to Muslims. The addition of 'prevent them from drinking wine' highlights the practical application of *radhāʿah* in mixed-faith households, ensuring social and ritual boundaries are maintained even when the nurse is non-Muslim. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the act of nursing itself, rather than the faith of the nurse, creates the permanent familial bond.
